thread:
ravi: Noticing River13b-int4 canary hitting allocation races when many short-turn chats request long continues (>700). latency spikes and intermittent OOMs.
tess: timeline?
ravi: started around 02:10UTC after traffic shift. example log: 

```
[2026-03-22T02:12:34Z] alloc_warn: failed_contiguous_alloc 2.0GB need for kv_chunk
[2026-03-22T02:12:34Z] kv_manager: prefetch_pages=40 page_size=64KB
[2026-03-22T02:12:34Z] batch: active=10 max_new_tokens=800
[2026-03-22T02:12:34Z] allocator: largest_free=780MB free_segments=28
```

tess: different from fp16?
omar: yes fp16 ok. int4's tighter memory and page layout plus prefetch is the combo.
sylvia: propose three-step triage: A) soft throttle for long-gen traffic, B) compaction-on-alloc retry (with timeout), C) bounded prefetch per-request.
ravi: I sketched a minimal change set to toggle via model config: 

```
models:
  river13b-int4:
    defaults:
      max_new_tokens: 400
      prefetch_policy: bounded
      prefetch_bytes_limit: 131072
    runtime:
      compaction_on_alloc_ms: 10
      long_gen_batch_cap: 7
```

sylvia: compaction_on_alloc_ms=10 means background defrag attempt for up to 10ms before retrying alloc? SRE concerns: CPU jitter.
tess: small CPU hit but prevents expensive OOMs and rollbacks. need a knob to disable on heavy-CPU hosts.
omar: implement a fast-path: if alloc fails and compaction_on_alloc_ms>0 then launch compactor thread that runs lightweight coalesce for up to N iterations, then retry alloc once. fallback to model-variant if still fails.
deploy-bot: deploy started river13b-int4 canary (uid: 9f5d1)
ravi: initial canary 15m: p95 down 22%, 2 alloc-failures converted to successful retries, no hard OOMs.
sylvia: added metrics: allocator.compaction_retries_total, allocator.compaction_time_ms,prefetch.bytes_per_request. wired alerts if compaction_retries_total>5/min.
tess: also created routing rule: requests with explicit max_new_tokens>=1024 route to dedicated-large pool.
omar: evaluating quality: reducing default max_new_tokens to 400 affects very long completions, but traffic analysis shows <1% of calls requested >400 originally. customers requesting >400 should be directed to large-pool or increase quota.
sylvia: follow-up ticket to revisit allocator: try slab merging when free neighboring chunks present, and change page allocation pattern to avoid issuing large contiguous requests.
ravi: I'll document change in onboarding playbook and send quick note to platform-users. If canary stable for 3 hours, roll to stable with rollback plan. Thanks. :shipit:
